title: KV eviction heatmap experiment log and trace tagging primer
content:
Context:
This note records a short series of experiments (Oct->Nov 2024) exploring how KV cache eviction dynamics correlate with tail latency and token cost across multi-tenant inference. Goal is to produce a compact dashboard (heatmap + probe panels) and a minimal trace tag convention so operators can quickly find tenant/route-level cold-cache pain points without exploding trace cardinality.

Why this is different: many prior docs list metrics and dashboards; this is a focused experiment log with repeatable steps, SQL/metric derivations, and a tight span/tagging primer aimed at minimizing cardinality while preserving signal for root-cause.

Primary goals:
- Produce an infer-backed heatmap: x-axis = per-tenant KV eviction rate (5m), y-axis = 99th token latency (5m), color = requests-per-minute or token-cost-per-minute.
- Define a small set of derived metrics and trace tags that pin an event to (tenant, model-variant, route, kv_hit_bool) without adding high-cardinality keys like full prompt hashes.
- Run 3 experiment variants (baseline, reduced-eviction-policy, aggressive-prefetch) and capture success metrics.

Metric definitions (derivation notes):
- kv.evictions_per_min (tenant): count(kv_eviction_event{tenant}) / 1m window. Use counter delta on ingestion to avoid double-counting across shards.
- kv.hits_per_token (tenant): sum(kv_hits) / sum(tokens_generated) over window. Prefer rate(sum) for short windows.
- kv.warmth_p50/p75/p95 (tenant): distribution of cache hit latency upstream (proxy for locality). Compute from histogram buckets exported by runtime.
- request.token_latency_99 (route): 99th percentile of per-token generation time from serving runtime (exclude network hop).
- cost.rate_per_min (tenant): token_count * model_unit_cost (lookup per model) aggregated per minute.
- eviction-tail-contrib (route): correlation metric: covariance(kv.evictions_per_min, request.token_latency_99) normalized by variance(kv.evictions_per_min). Used to rank routes.

SQL/snippet examples (Prometheus-ish / analytics):
- kv evictions per tenant (PromQL):
  rate(kv_eviction_count_total{job="runtime"}[5m])

- p99 token latency per route (PromQL):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_generation_latency_bucket{job="runtime"}[5m])) by (le, route))

- eviction / p99 join (high-level):
  topk(50, by(route, tenant) ( (rate(kv_eviction_count_total[5m]) * 1.0) * on(route, tenant) group_left() histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_generation_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, tenant)) ))

Trace/span tagging primer (cardinality-conscious):
Design constraints: tags must answer "who, what, why" for an event but avoid freeform values. Avoid prompt/user IDs in high-card fields.
- base span name: "llm.infer"
- minimal tags (all strings/enums):
  - tenant: <tenant_id> (hashed short id, keep limited set)
  - model: <model_family> (e.g., gptx-13b, quant-4bit)
  - variant: <variant_tag> (can be "fallback"/"primary")
  - route: <api_route_enum> (one of a controlled set)
  - kv_hit: "true" | "false" (string boolean)
  - batch_size: "1","2-8","9-32","32+" (bucketed)
  - seq_len_bucket: "short","medium","long" (pre-defined buckets)
- lightweight annotations (not tags):
  - kv_eviction_hint: "evicted_prefix" | "kv_compaction" | "none" (small enum attached as annotation)
  - probe_marker: "probe-run-2024-11-07" (for correlating synthetic probes)

Span naming rationale: keep span.name generic so instrumented code can add low-cardinality tags for filtering. Avoid adding per-request ids as primary tag keys (they belong in logs / separate trace sampling payloads).

Dashboard wireframe notes (compact heatmap + drill panels):
1) Heatmap panel (main)
   - X axis: kv.evictions_per_min (log scale)
   - Y axis: request.token_latency_99 (ms)
   - Color: token_cost_per_min (gradient), point size by requests_per_min
   - Grouping / tooltip: tenant (short), route, model.
2) Top offenders table (right)
   - Columns: rank, tenant, route, evictions_per_min, p99_latency, kv.hits_per_token, cost.rate_per_min
   - Sort default by eviction-tail-contrib desc.
3) Trace-sample panel (bottom-left)
   - Show 3 sampled traces per offending (tenant,route) pair, with annotated kv_hit flags and probe_marker if present.
4) Probe cadence panel (bottom-right)
   - Synthetic probe success rate, median latency, kv_hit ratio for probe runs.

Experiment plan (steps):
- Baseline (Week 1): capture 2 weeks of existing signals with new derived metrics enabled (no policy changes).
- Variant A (Week 2): reduce eviction aggressiveness by increasing LRU threshold; measure change in kv.evictions_per_min and p99.
- Variant B (Week 3): enable aggressive prefetch for top 10 routes (heuristic: highest eviction-tail-contrib).
- For each variant: collect heatmap snapshots, top offenders, and 200 trace samples for later human review.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Variant A reduces kv.evictions_per_min by >= 30% for top 50 offenders and reduces request.token_latency_99 by >= 10% for those routes, without increasing cost.rate_per_min > 8%.
- Variant B reduces p99 by >= 20% on targeted routes with cost increase limited to 12% and no regression in other tenants.

Open questions / risks:
- Cardinailty: tenant tag is necessary, but tenants with very low volume will create noise in heatmap. Proposal: cap top-N and aggregate rest as "other-small-tenants".
- Sampling bias: trace sampling should weight on kv_hit=false to surface cold-cache stacks; default sampler currently uniform. Need sampler config PR (see linked PR).
- Billing signal: per-model unit costs are in a separate pricing table that isn't in telemetry; need join downstream to compute cost.rate_per_min accurately.

Operational runbook snippet (if heatmap triggers):
1) If eviction-tail-contrib > threshold for a route, open incident stub with owner (platform/route owner).
2) Attach 10 traces and heatmap snapshot.
3) Check reachback: were there recent rollouts for model or routing changes? link to rollout id in panel.
4) Temporary mitigation: bump cache TTL for tenant-route or enable prefetch for top offending model bucket.

Next steps / action items:
- [ ] Isha to wire PromQL panels and create the initial dashboard skeleton (due 2024-11-01).
- [ ] Miguel to add sampler-weight change in runtime PR and link sampling config (PR #897 referenced).
- [ ] Riley to run baseline capture and produce heatmap snapshots (due 2024-11-07).
- [ ] Jun to prototype the top-offenders ranker and eviction-tail-contrib script in analytics (SQL notebook).

Notes to self / rough ideas: keep the heatmap visually dense but semantically sparse — operators should be able to answer "is this eviction problem localized or systemic" within 30s of looking. Try colorblind-friendly palettes.

Appendix (short glossary):
- KV warmth: heuristic for local cache locality (higher is better).
- Eviction: runtime event when an entry is removed from KV cache due to space policy or TTL.
- Probe: synthetic inference request designed to measure cache warmth for a target route/tenant.

End of experiment log.
